findings.text: The first sentence clearly says what Athena is and how it works, so a newcomer can name the product immediately. It does not say what problem this solves or who it is for, so 'why it matters' rests only on the demonstration that follows.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The page explains why a study of another project is on Athena's site, which stops the reader wondering why Athena's address opens on firstmate. However, the study shows Athena reading code, which is not the request-to-change workflow described in the sentence before it.
findings.source: Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files.

findings.text: A next step appears in the header and links to a 'Next steps' section with the Athena repository. A newcomer knows what to do without scrolling through the rest of the page.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The study id and folder are internal detail that a first-time reader does not need in the opening paragraphs. They add weight before the reader reaches the content.
findings.source: Its study id, firstmate-work-handling, is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from.

findings.text: The 'Start here' section defines terms before they are used, then gives a numbered walk through one task. This makes the firstmate content followable even for someone who has never seen firstmate.

After 'Start here', most of the page is a dense spec of firstmate: 11 transition cards, design-choice cards ra1 to ra6, a glossary and 44 claims. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena gets very little more about Athena from this part.
The opening promises that a second model checks the work and that costs are recorded, but the page shows neither for this study. A newcomer cannot see those features in action.
findings.source: has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: The findings listed are f1, f3 and f4, with no f2 and no note about why. A careful reader may wonder what was left out.

Some card text uses words the page never explains before they appear. 'Harness' is only defined in the glossary, and 'endpoint' and 'pin' (in this sense) are not explained at that point. Those passages are hard going for a newcomer.
findings.source: A ship or scout keeps its recorded harness and needs a note; a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none, and a secondmate with no endpoint is recovered by the spawn script instead.
